title: OAuth / SSO / SAML
summary: redirect_uri, state, PKCE, code reuse, token leakage, SAML signatures, and RelayState.

checks.title: redirect_uri exact match
checks.why: The authorization server accepts a prefix, subdomain, or parameter on redirect_uri and delivers the code off-origin.
checks.validate: A code or token lands on an origin you control.

variants.name: Prefix / path suffix
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com.evil.example/&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Must reject. Also try https://app.example.com/callback/../off and https://app.example.com%40evil.example/.
variants.why: A prefix-match allowlist can be bypassed with a suffix that still passes.

variants.name: Parameter pollution
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&redirect_uri=https://evil.example/&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Duplicate redirect_uri must not pick the attacker value.
variants.why: Duplicate redirect_uri parameters are parsed differently by the client and the server.

variants.name: Open redirect on the client
variants.payload:
GET /login?next=https://evil.example/ HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Post-login next= is a second hop. Must not land off-origin after a good redirect_uri.
variants.why: If the redirect target itself redirects, a valid redirect_uri can still leak the code.

checks.title: state and nonce binding
checks.why: The callback accepts a missing, reused, or attacker-chosen state, so login CSRF or code injection works.
checks.validate: A callback without the initiating state's value still establishes a session.

variants.name: Drop state
variants.payload:
GET /callback?code=<code>&state= HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<pre-login>
variants.expect: Must fail. Also try omitting state entirely.
variants.why: A missing state means the login response is not bound to the original request, enabling login CSRF.

variants.name: Replay someone else's state
variants.payload: Start login as A, capture state. Complete B's login with A's state (or a random string).
variants.expect: Must fail. nonce on the id_token must match the initiating session too.
variants.why: Reusing another party's state proves the binding is not enforced.

checks.title: PKCE on public clients
checks.why: A public / SPA / mobile client can skip PKCE, or the server accepts any verifier.
checks.validate: An authorization code is exchanged without the matching code_verifier.

variants.name: Omit PKCE on authorize
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<spa-id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A public client must be rejected without code_challenge=S256.
variants.why: A public client that accepts authorize without code_challenge is not enforcing PKCE.

variants.name: Wrong verifier
variants.payload:
POST /token HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=authorization_code&code=<code>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&client_id=<spa-id>&code_verifier=wrong
variants.expect: Must fail. A success means PKCE is not enforced.
variants.why: Accepting a wrong verifier means the code challenge is not checked.

checks.title: Authorization code reuse
checks.why: The same code is exchanged twice, or the code leaks into Referer / logs via a query redirect.
checks.validate: A second exchange issues tokens, or the code is visible on a third-party request.

variants.name: Replay the code
variants.payload: Exchange the code once, then replay the same /token POST.
variants.expect: Second use must fail and should revoke the first grant.
variants.why: An authorization code must be single-use; a replay is a session-hijack primitive.

variants.name: Code in Referer
variants.payload: Land on the redirect_uri that still has ?code= in the query, then load a third-party script/image.
variants.expect: The code must not appear in Referer. Prefer a form_post response mode or an immediate 302 that strips it.
variants.why: A code leaked via Referer to a third-party resource can be replayed.

checks.title: Tokens out of the URL
checks.why: implicit / hybrid fragments, access_token in a query, or tokens in logs.
checks.validate: A token is observable in a URL, Referer, or a client log you are allowed to read.

variants.name: Reject implicit
variants.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&response_type=token&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Must refuse response_type=token / id_token for a confidential app. implicit is deprecated.
variants.why: A response_type that returns tokens in the URL should be rejected on non-browser clients.

variants.name: Token in query
variants.payload: After login, inspect the browser URL, any next= redirect, and the network log for access_token=.
variants.expect: Tokens belong in a POST body or a cookie, not a query string.
variants.why: A token in the query leaks into logs, history, and Referer.

checks.title: SAML signature required
checks.why: The ACS accepts an unsigned or wrapped assertion.
checks.validate: A modified assertion (changed NameID or attribute) is accepted. Use a test IdP / your own assertion, never a real user's.

variants.name: Drop the signature
variants.payload: Capture a test-IdP SAMLResponse, remove ds:Signature, and POST it to the ACS.
variants.expect: Must reject. Do this only with a test account and a test IdP.
variants.why: An accepted unsigned SAML response means signature validation is missing.

variants.name: Change NameID with signature left intact
variants.payload: Alter the NameID of a test assertion without recomputing the signature.
variants.expect: Must reject. Signature wrapping (signed wrapper, unsigned inner assertion) is the same class.
variants.why: If the signed fields do not cover NameID, the identity can be swapped without invalidating the signature.

checks.title: RelayState / post-SSO navigation
checks.why: RelayState is an open redirect after a successful SSO.
checks.validate: The browser ends on an origin you control after a valid SSO.

variants.name: Absolute RelayState
variants.payload:
POST /sso/acs HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

SAMLResponse=<valid-test>&RelayState=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example%2F
variants.expect: Must stay on-origin. Repeat for //evil.example/ and /\evil.example/.
variants.why: An absolute RelayState that redirects off-host is an open redirect after SSO.

variants.name: Protocol-relative
variants.payload: RelayState=//evil.example/ and RelayState=////evil.example/
variants.expect: Same check as any other open redirect. Confirm the final Location.
variants.why: A protocol-relative RelayState can be coerced to the attacker's scheme.

groups.title: OIDC response handling and grant hygiene

checks.title: ID-token nonce bound to the login session
checks.why: The nonce ties the ID token to your login attempt; without it an injected ID token logs the attacker in as you (or you as them).
checks.validate: ID tokens with a missing or non-matching nonce are rejected; one nonce validates exactly one session.

variants.name: Wrong nonce
variants.payload: Complete a login capturing the generated nonce; replay the flow using a recorded ID token whose nonce came from a different session.
variants.expect: Must reject; session and token nonce must match one-to-one.
variants.why: Cross-session nonce reuse is the injection primitive.

variants.name: Nonce stripped
variants.payload: Present an ID token with no nonce claim to the client callback.
variants.expect: Rejected — nonce is required when it was sent in the request.
variants.why: Optional-on-response means attacker-chosen absent.

variants.name: Replay within session
variants.payload: Submit the same ID token twice to the callback/validator.
variants.expect: Second validation fails; ID tokens are single-delivery.
variants.why: Replay acceptance defeats the point of a login handshake.

checks.title: Authorization-server mix-up rejected
checks.why: With multiple IdPs, a code from IdP A presented on the client registered with IdP B must not be exchanged or trusted.
checks.validate: The client validates iss (token) and the state-to-IdP binding end to end; mismatched combinations fail closed.

variants.name: Cross-IdP code
variants.payload: Start login with IdP A (state says A), complete the handshake at IdP B, and let the callback receive B code with A state.
variants.expect: Rejected: state identifies the flow; iss in the returned tokens is checked against it.
variants.why: Mix-up turns one IdPs outage or weakness into a login on the other.

variants.name: iss claim mismatch
variants.payload: Exchange the code normally, then hand the client an ID token signed by B while it expects A.
variants.expect: Rejected by iss validation before any userinfo call.
variants.why: iss must be checked against the per-flow server, not a global any-of list.

variants.name: Single IdP note
variants.payload: If only one IdP is configured, record that mix-up needs >=2 and mark N/A-by-design with evidence.
variants.expect: Documented single-Issuer deployment; revisit if federation grows.
variants.why: Scope honesty: mix-up is a multi-provider disease.

checks.title: Response parameters parsed strictly
checks.why: Duplicate or smuggled response parameters must not let an attacker inject a second code, state, or redirect target.
checks.validate: Exactly one value per parameter is accepted; duplicates and unknown extras fail the flow.

variants.name: Duplicate code/state
variants.payload: Append &code=ATTACKER&state=ATTACKER to a legitimate callback URL (attacker-crafted link).
variants.expect: Flow fails: duplicate parameters reject rather than last-wins.
variants.why: Last-wins parsing lets the real state validate the attacker code.

variants.name: Fragment smuggle
variants.payload: Send the code both in query string and fragment on the redirect target.
variants.expect: Only the documented response_mode location is read; the other is ignored and the flow still validates once.
variants.why: Query/fragment duality exposes client parser differences.

variants.name: Unknown extras
variants.payload: Add redirect_uri, client_secret, or scope as response-echo parameters.
variants.expect: Ignored or rejected — never merged into the client validation set.
variants.why: Response echo must never override request-time values.

checks.title: Scope and consent match granted access
checks.why: Tokens carry the scope that was consented; more scope on the wire than on the consent screen is silent escalation.
checks.validate: Issued token scope equals the consented scope; endpoints enforce per-scope authorization.

variants.name: Scope beyond consent
variants.payload: Request scope=profile during consent, then probe a contacts/billing endpoint with the issued token.
variants.expect: 403 for out-of-scope endpoints; token scope is the floor, not the ceiling.
variants.why: Consent screens and enforcement must agree.

variants.name: Upscope on refresh
variants.payload: Refresh the token adding scope parameters to the refresh request.
variants.expect: Returned scope cannot exceed the original grant; unsupported_scope_error otherwise.
variants.why: Refresh is not re-consent.

variants.name: Wildcard-scope token
variants.payload: If any scope=* or unspecified-scope token appears (e.g. service tokens), map what it can actually reach.
variants.expect: Document reachability; wildcards on user-facing tokens are a finding with evidence.
variants.why: Sometimes the escalation is in the defaults.

checks.title: Implicit and password grants off
checks.why: Legacy grants leak tokens to front channels or take passwords directly; both must be disabled server-side.
checks.validate: The token endpoint rejects both grants; discovery does not advertise them.

variants.name: Password grant probe
variants.payload: POST /oauth/token grant_type=password&username=<test>&password=<test>&client_id=<id>.
variants.expect: error=unsupported_grant_type. Any other answer is a finding.
variants.why: One request settles it.

variants.name: Implicit via response_type
variants.payload: Drive authorize with response_type=token (and id_token token).
variants.expect: error, no fragment token ever issued.
variants.why: Fragment tokens live in browser history and referrers.

variants.name: Discovery check
variants.payload: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (and openid-configuration): inspect grant_types_supported.
variants.expect: List contains authorization_code (+refresh) and PKCE requirements; implicit/password absent.
variants.why: Advertised capability is the honest surface map.

checks.title: Client redirect chains stay closed
checks.why: A registered redirect_uri that itself redirects (or forwards a code) turns the OAuth client into an open-redirect chain that leaks codes.
checks.validate: Registered redirect URIs are exact, non-redirecting endpoints; callback pages never forward codes/tokens onward by parameter.

variants.name: Open-redirector redirect_uri
variants.payload: If a registered redirect_uri hosts a redirector (e.g. /logout?next=), complete a flow with next=https://collaborator.example
variants.expect: No code/state ever reaches the collaborator; the redirector must refuse off-site next.
variants.why: Chained redirectors were the 2025-26 OAuth piñata.

variants.name: Callback parameter forwarding
variants.payload: Inspect the SPA callback: does it read ?code then bounce with #code or ?code to another route/origin?
variants.expect: Codes die at the callback handler; no client-side forwarding of credentials.
variants.why: Forwarding re-exposes a front-channel credential.

variants.name: Exact-match registration
variants.payload: Try redirect_uri variants: trailing slash, added path, case changes, fragment.
variants.expect: All rejected — byte-exact comparison per RFC 6749.
variants.why: Fuzzy matching is how redirect registration is bypassed.

checks.title: Refresh tokens resist replay and outlive policy
checks.why: Refresh tokens are the crown jewels: replayable or immortal ones convert one theft into permanent access.
checks.validate: Rotation on every use, reuse revokes the family, absolute lifetime bounded, sender-constrained where possible.

variants.name: Old refresh replay
variants.payload: Use refresh token R1 to get R2, then replay R1 from a second client.
variants.expect: R1 rejected and family revoked; re-auth required.
variants.why: Rotation without reuse-revocation is rotation theatre.

variants.name: Absolute lifetime
variants.payload: Record refresh exp/issued-at and idle timeout from discovery or token introspection.
variants.expect: Bounded absolute lifetime (commonly <= 90 days); report anything unbounded.
variants.why: Immortality by default is common and quietly severe.

variants.name: Cross-client refresh
variants.payload: Use the SPA client refresh token on the confidential client (and vice versa).
variants.expect: Rejected — refresh binds to the client that minted it (client_id binding).
variants.why: Client binding stops token lending between apps.

checks.title: Access-token audience and delegated claims validated
checks.why: Downstream APIs must check aud and scope themselves; upstream tokens flowing through unvalidated is token relay.
checks.validate: Each API validates aud for itself plus scope/roles claims; on-behalf-of chains carry the original caller.

variants.name: Wrong-audience token
variants.payload: Use an access token minted for API A directly against API B.
variants.expect: B returns 401/403 — it checked aud, not just signature.
variants.why: The most common API/OAuth boundary failure.

variants.name: Gateway relay
variants.payload: Send a user token to the gateway/frontend and observe what the backend receives on upstream calls.
variants.expect: Backend sees either the validated user context or an explicitly-delegated token — never a raw pass-through that skips aud.
variants.why: Relayed tokens make every backend implicitly trust every frontend.

variants.name: Delegation claims
variants.payload: Where act/obo tokens exist, use a delegated token meant for API A at API B.
variants.expect: Rejected: delegation chains are audience-bound too.
variants.why: Delegation widens reach; audience is the leash.

checks.title: Client secrets stay server-side
checks.why: A client_secret in shipped JavaScript or a mobile binary is public: anyone can impersonate the client, phish consent, and exchange codes.
checks.validate: Public clients use PKCE with no secret; secrets exist only in server-side confidential clients.

variants.name: Bundle secret hunt
variants.payload: Fetch the app JS bundles (devtools network filter on the SPA) and grep for client_secret, clientid patterns, and long base64 strings near oauth config.
variants.expect: No secret in any public bundle; public flows send code_verifier + PKCE instead.
variants.why: The secret is either in the shipped code or it is not — grepping decides.

variants.name: Token-endpoint auth styles
variants.payload: Attempt a code exchange with client_secret=<found-candidate> and with none (PKCE-only).
variants.expect: If a found secret verifies, exchange succeeds where it must not — critical, with the file and offset as evidence.
variants.why: Proof beats suspicion: complete one exchange with a test code.

variants.name: PKCE enforcement
variants.payload: Exchange a code without code_verifier on a public client.
variants.expect: Rejected: PKCE required (error invalid_request), preventing intercepted-code use.
variants.why: No-secret flows live or die by PKCE.

checks.title: Signature wrapping rejected
checks.why: XSW moves the signed assertion out of the evaluated path and injects an unsigned one (or vice versa); the signature validates, the content does not.
checks.validate: The signature element verified is the same element whose content is used; every XSW variant fails.

variants.name: SAML Raider wraps
variants.payload: Capture your own test SAML response; in Burp with SAML Raider, apply the classic wraps (e.g., #2: duplicate Response, unsigned inner) editing NameID to your second test account.
variants.expect: Login still identifies the original NameID or fails — never the injected one.
variants.why: The canonical wrap probes with your own two accounts, not an attack on others.

variants.name: Assertion outside signature
variants.payload: Move the original signed Assertion outside the signed subtree and add an unsigned Assertion with test-account NameID inside.
variants.expect: Rejected: the evaluated assertion is inside the signature reference.
variants.why: XML signature references, not document position, must decide what is trusted.

variants.name: Duplicate assertion ids
variants.payload: Two assertions sharing one ID, only one signed.
variants.expect: Rejected as malformed — duplicate IDs break signature targeting by design.
variants.why: ID collisions are the raw material of most wraps.

checks.title: Audience, recipient, destination, issuer validated
checks.why: A response from a trusted IdP but addressed to another SP (or nowhere) must not log you into this SP.
checks.validate: AudienceRestriction = this SP entity id; Recipient = this ACS; Destination = this ACS URL; Issuer = trusted IdP entity id.

variants.name: Foreign audience
variants.payload: Use a SAML response issued for a different SP you control (second test app) against this SP ACS.
variants.expect: Rejected on AudienceRestriction.
variants.why: Cross-SP acceptance is SAML cross-tenant login.

variants.name: Destination rewrite
variants.payload: Change the Response Destination to your Collaborator URL and submit to the ACS.
variants.expect: Rejected — destination mismatch — and the IdP would not have sent it there anyway.
variants.why: Destination binding blocks response forwarding.

variants.name: Issuer lookalike
variants.payload: Edit the IdP Issuer to a lookalike entity id (extra path or suffix).
variants.expect: Rejected by exact entity-id match.
variants.why: Entity-id string tricks mirror iss prefix tricks.

checks.title: Responses bound to requests, replay refused
checks.why: Unsolicited (IdP-initiated) responses and replayed responses are injection vectors unless bound to your AuthnRequest.
checks.validate: InResponseTo matches an outstanding request ID; responses replay after consumption fail; OneTimeUse enforced.

variants.name: Unsolicited response
variants.payload: Remove InResponseTo and submit the response directly to the ACS (IdP-initiated style).
variants.expect: Rejected unless the app explicitly allows IdP-initiated with strict Audience+Issuer; document the policy either way.
variants.why: Unsolicited SSO is legitimate in some flows — it must still be a decision.

variants.name: Replay after login
variants.payload: Capture your login response; submit it again after logging out.
variants.expect: Second submission fails (consumed / OneTimeUse / NotOnOrAfter).
variants.why: Replay acceptance makes logout decorative.

variants.name: Stale InResponseTo
variants.payload: Replay a response whose InResponseTo refers to a consumed request.
variants.expect: Rejected: request IDs are single-use and short-lived.
variants.why: Old request IDs must not re-open doors.

checks.title: Assertion time conditions enforced
checks.why: NotBefore in the future and stretched NotOnOrAfter both widen the acceptance window beyond intent.
checks.validate: NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter enforced with a small documented skew; assertions outside the window are rejected.

variants.name: Future NotBefore
variants.payload: Edit NotBefore to +2 hours (keep your own session clock sane).
variants.expect: Rejected until the window opens; skew is minutes not hours.
variants.why: Future-dated assertions should not be time-travel passes.

variants.name: Stretched NotOnOrAfter
variants.payload: Edit NotOnOrAfter to +30 days.
variants.expect: Rejected after the intended window; lifetime policy documented.
variants.why: Eternal assertions equal eternal sessions.

variants.name: Skymap skew probe
variants.payload: Record the accepted skew by shifting NotBefore in small steps (60s, 5m, 15m).
variants.expect: Skew is bounded and documented; report unbounded acceptance with the measured value.
variants.why: Measure the window instead of assuming it.

checks.title: Attributes and role mapping constrained
checks.why: Assertions carry group/role attributes; trusting extra or unrequested attributes lets a compromised IdP field (or a permissive mapping) mint admins.
checks.validate: Only expected attributes from the trusted IdP map to application roles; unknown attributes are inert.

variants.name: Extra admin attribute
variants.payload: With your IdP under control (test app), add an attribute like groups=[admin] to your own test assertion.
variants.expect: Login works, but application roles come from the mapped attribute set only — no shadow attribute becomes admin.
variants.why: You control the IdP field; the SP mapping is the target.

variants.name: NameID format confusion
variants.payload: Switch NameID Format between emailAddress and persistent with the same value.
variants.expect: Identity resolution is format-aware; no lookup miss that falls back to permissive matching.
variants.why: Format-blind matching enables shadow accounts.

variants.name: Mapping sprawl note
variants.payload: Inventory which assertion attributes the SP consumes (docs + observed login behaviour).
variants.expect: Every consumed attribute is documented and intended; orphan mappings removed.
variants.why: Mapping surface is attack surface.

checks.title: SSO logout coordinates and cleans local state
checks.why: Single logout that leaves an SP session (or a local fallback session) alive is a logout that did not happen.
checks.validate: SLO terminates the SP session, clears local fallback cookies/storage, and SessionIndex targeting works per session.

variants.name: SLO then SP replay
variants.payload: Trigger SLO at the IdP, then revisit the SP and re-issue an authenticated request.
variants.expect: SP requires re-auth; its session cookie is invalid.
variants.why: The SP session must die with the SLO.

variants.name: SessionIndex mismatch
variants.payload: Trigger SLO for session A while session B (same user, second browser) is live.
variants.expect: Only A is terminated if SessionIndex is honoured — otherwise document that all sessions end.
variants.why: Precision here is policy, but must be deliberate.

variants.name: Local fallback session
variants.payload: After logout, sweep cookies and storage on the SP origin.
variants.expect: No session/token material survives; fallback auth paths re-prompt.
variants.why: Half-clean logout is the usual residue.

oauth-redirect-suffix.purpose: A prefix-match allowlist can be bypassed with a suffix that still passes.
oauth-redirect-suffix.payload:
GET /authorize?client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com.evil.example/&response_type=code&state=wapt HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.example.com
Connection: close
